name: Scholar drop in bucket
description:
Select and drop a selection of items into one of several buckets- many to many match to replace drag and drops.
This allows you to set up a questions with n number of categories each of which can receive up to x number of answers in any order as long as they are under the correct category.

You can format the layout of the buckets by use of HTML.
To create extra spaces in a bucket (or to keep all buckets of an even size) you can use empty items.

You can create distractors to have extra drop items.
Items can be dropped in any of teh lcaotions in their bucket.

hint.value: Select an item and then select where you would like to place it.

marking_script:
mark:
if(interpreted_answer = 0, incorrect("Incorrect. Try again?"),
if(interpreted_answer < input_options['how_many_matches'],if (input_options['all_or_nothing'],incorrect("You must find all matches to get the marks") , apply(partial_feedback)),correct("Correct."));end())

interpreted_answer:
studentAnswer

mark_per_gap:
marks/input_options["how_many_matches"]

partial_feedback:
set_credit((interpreted_answer/input_options['how_many_matches']) , "Partially correct."); end()

settings.name: drop_zone
settings.label: Drop zone with items
settings.hint:
Design the categories.

'Buckets' are defined Using @[ bucket ]@

'Items' are contained within the brackets of the bucket, and defined using%[ item]%

Use blank items to control the number of slots in each bucket.

You can use html markup to add images, align and style text etc.
Capitalisation does not work in this type - for capitlisation/drag to sentence use the 1-2-1 drop on targe question,
